payload.title: Sign in to Papyrus CLI with Google and select the authorized publication
payload.description:
Issue filing only, explicitly requested by Ryan. No implementation, login, new credentials, security/configuration changes or deployment is authorized. Parent epic: PPY-7c458d71-3ea8-4c39-8a6c-d2d2ab903df7. Reference: Apricity authorization-code+PKCE login, keychain refresh session and renewal, https://github.com/AnthusAI/Apricity/blob/ffe8a023b0418445aa67893a52ae9e173c366d42/crates/apricity-cli/src/cloud.rs#L206. Preserve existing newsroom authorization and agent attribution; do not conflate CLI auth with hosted procedure execution.

As a newsroom user I can run papyrus login using normal Google/newsroom identity so editorial CLI commands use my existing permissions without a personal AWS SSO session.

Feature: Normal newsroom CLI identity
  Scenario: First Google login
    Given a configured supported publication OAuth client and an authorized newsroom user
    And no personal AWS credentials or SSO session
    When the user runs papyrus login and completes Google sign-in in the system browser
    Then the CLI reports the verified person and publication
    And code+PKCE/state and a registered loopback callback protect the flow
    And no password, token or client secret is printed or requested in chat
  Scenario: Select a publication with existing permission
    Given a signed-in user with account/publication grants
    When the user selects a publication and requests a protected action
    Then the server checks current grants and the exact tenant/resource binding
    And absent, revoked or stale grants deny the action without broader IAM fallback
    And ambiguous selection is resolved explicitly rather than guessed

Coordinate API trust/permission boundary and intentional IAM-only CLI policy revision with PPY-58f1 before implementation. Do not infer a new native client is already registered or accepted by existing APIs. Acceptance evidence must include real user-permission parity and negative cross-publication tests, with identity distinct from content author/agent metadata.
